target_customer: Consumers with sleep and wake-up problems who own smartphones
problem: Alarms wake people mid sleep cycle, leaving them groggy.
business_model: Consumer hardware, about $50 to $60 wristband sold direct

founders.name: Arun Gupta
education: Yale student (dropped out per Startup Foundry)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists founder of KCRG Inc., Grailed and Wakemate; Wikipedia says Yale student

founders.name: Greg Nemeth
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in TechCrunch November 2009; not on YC page

exit.reason: Gupta wrote on June 27, 2012 that the company had exhausted its capital and would stop making WakeMates

competitors.name: Zeo Personal Sleep Coach
competitors.what: Headband measuring brainwaves with alarm clock

technical_complexity.rationale: Hardware wristband with accelerometer, Bluetooth sync to many phone platforms and server analytics; shipping delays, Android compatibility problems and a charger recall in December 2010 show the difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Actigraphy is a well established technique; the cheap band was copyable by Fitbit, Jawbone and others.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Zeo, Lark, Fitbit, Nike+ and Jawbone UP were named as rivals by 2012; no acquisition of WakeMate occurred.

market_need_then: Smart alarms and sleep tracking had a niche audience in 2009; Zeo had just launched at about $250, and WakeMate offered a cheaper band at about $50 with preorders in November 2009.

identity.voice_and_tone: Short promo page presents WakeMate as an idea about paying attention to your sleep rhythm

branding.community_and_virality: Press and a Startup Foundry interview; no merch or fan activity found.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly descriptive name; coverage from TechCrunch and Engadget existed but no brand assets or community were found. A 2012 episode where a cofounder used the WakeMate email list for MiLife+ shows the list was valuable.

outcome_analysis: WakeMate shipped late in 2010, then suffered Android compatibility problems and a December 2010 charger recall. In June 2012 the CEO said capital was exhausted and production stopped, while a cofounder dispute over the MiLife+ campaign added turmoil. Rivals Zeo, Fitbit and Jawbone grew in the same period.
notes: CB Insights reports $20K over 3 rounds from 4 investors, seed dated 2009-06-26; this rests on a single database and Seedtable shows no rounds, so the amount and investor list are unverified. Wikipedia says Perfect Third was founded December 2009 and lists later team members. Competitors Aug 2009 sources absent; Zeo sourced November 2009 (five months after batch start). Wakemate.com is a promo landing page.
